name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,783

entries.clue: A day char regularly spent going to continent (6)

indicators.note: every other letter of 'char' is used up, leaving the rest at regular intervals

annotation.surface: A cleaner's day off is spent travelling abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like the British cleaning lady (a charwoman); here it is only letters to be thinned out.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Africa is one of the seven continents, the second largest.

entries.clue: Freshened beer for dog (8)

blocks.note: a room is aired, i.e. freshened

annotation.surface: Topping up a dog's bowl with fresh beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Freshened beer' reads as one phrase about a drink, but it splits into two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.

entries.clue: Batman initially held by wrongly arrested Robin (9)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of 'Batman'
B is held inside the rearranged letters
the letters of 'arrested' are set out wrongly, i.e. rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of Batman, placed after RED

annotation.surface: Batman is locked up after Robin is wrongfully arrested.
annotation.walkthrough: The Batman-and-Robin surface makes Robin the sidekick; in the answer it is the bird, and the capital R hides that.
annotation.definitionFit: Redbreast is an old name for the robin, from its red chest.

entries.clue: Scrawnier, oddly deficient stick (4)

indicators.note: the word lacks its odd-numbered letters, so only the even ones remain

annotation.surface: A thin, weirdly lacking stick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' does not mean strangely here: it tells you to drop the odd letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the woody stem of bamboo or rattan, cut to length, is what people lean on or beat with.

entries.clue: Quietly steal around two mushrooms (8)

indicators.note: SH and TAKE sit around the II

annotation.surface: Someone sneaking off with a couple of mushrooms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quietly steal' reads as one action, but the two words split apart and wrap the Roman numeral between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Shiitake are an East Asian edible mushroom; the word serves as its own plural.

entries.clue: Son in stew going to fashionable night club (3,4)

indicators.note: 'Son in stew' puts the son literally inside the pot, so S is enclosed by the stew word

blocks.note: a hotpot is a meat-and-potato stew, as in Lancashire hotpot

annotation.surface: A boy, in a state, heading off to a trendy club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In stew' suggests being flustered; it is literal: a hotpot is a British stew, and S goes in it.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a place where the action is, used especially of a buzzing venue everyone wants to be seen in.

entries.clue: Breach popular group around end of dinner (10)

indicators.note: 'Around' means surrounding, so the group word is placed on both sides of the letter that follows
take the last letter of 'dinner'

blocks.note: a faction is a group within a party

annotation.surface: A popular band gatecrashes the end of a dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popular group' looks like a pop band; it is two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name the breaking of a rule or law, from Latin for breaking.

entries.clue: Excuse from Crystal, "I bilked" (5)

indicators.note: the answer comes from within the following words

annotation.surface: Someone called Crystal offering a lame excuse for cheating people.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it sound like Crystal's confession; the answer runs across the name and the quote.
annotation.definitionFit: An alibi is an excuse, especially a claim of being elsewhere.

entries.clue: Quixotic former queen going to rave (6)

annotation.surface: An idealistic old queen heads out to a rave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rave' suggests a dance party; it is the verb, to rant. ER is Elizabeth II, now a former queen.
annotation.definitionFit: Don Quixote was the knight-errant, so errant means wandering in search of adventure.

entries.clue: Calling race (6)

blocks.note: a verb here: to rush along out of control

annotation.surface: A commentator calling a race.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words look like a race commentary; each is a separate meaning of the answer, which as a verb means to hurtle.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a vocation followed for life, and a verb for hurtling headlong, as a runaway cart does.

entries.clue: Unemployed 23 unfortunately losing seconds (9)

indicators.note: the letters end up badly arranged, i.e. rearranged
what the word is losing goes missing from it, so one S is taken out

blocks.note: s = second; one S is removed, leaving UNDERTAND to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone who has lost their job fails to grasp it all quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: A number in a clue stands for another answer, here UNDERSTAND from 23 across.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone made redundant has lost their job because it is no longer needed.

entries.clue: Religious man is distant hiding heart of purist (5)

indicators.note: something hiding a thing keeps it inside, out of sight, so the distance word wraps the letters
the middle two letters of 'purist'

annotation.surface: A monk keeps aloof while secretly a zealot at heart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Purist' has six letters, so its heart is the middle pair.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a member of a mendicant order such as the Franciscans, the word coming from Latin frater, brother.

entries.clue: Front of deserted vessel is gloomy (4)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'deserted'

annotation.surface: The bow of an abandoned ship looks grim.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Front' sounds nautical here, the bow of the ship; it just means the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe a place short of light, or a mood short of cheer.

entries.clue: Office worker by terminus perhaps lacking initial appeal (10)

indicators.note: STATION loses its first letter

blocks.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
a terminus is a kind of station; drop the S

annotation.surface: A temp commuting to the end of the line without much charm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks terminus as one example of a station.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the pull or allure something exerts on you, as in the appeal of a cream cake.

entries.clue: Whips around meeting genuine craft person (10)

indicators.note: the letters of 'whips' are moved around

blocks.note: right = genuine, as in the right stuff

annotation.surface: A whip-cracking boss inspecting a real artisan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Craft person' looks like a craftsman; the craft is a ship, and a shipwright builds them.
annotation.definitionFit: A shipwright builds ships, which are craft.

entries.clue: Thrash king hiding article (7)

indicators.note: something hiding a thing keeps it inside, out of sight, so the king wraps the article

annotation.surface: Beating a king for concealing a piece of writing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' tempts as the definition, since a hiding is a thrashing; here it is only the container signal, and 'Thrash' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To leather someone is to thrash them, originally with a leather strap.

entries.clue: Irritable heads of TV entertainment taking care hiring youths (6)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each following word

blocks.clueFragment: TV entertainment taking care hiring youths
blocks.note: T-V E-ntertainment T-aking C-are H-iring Y-ouths

annotation.surface: Grumpy television bosses fussing over hiring young presenters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heads of TV' reads as executives; it means the initial letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly British: easily annoyed and quick to snap, like a short-tempered boss.

entries.clue: Hot oil pool flowing by island riff-raff (3,6)

indicators.note: the letters of 'oil pool' run into a new order
'by' means next to, so the island letter is simply placed beside the rest

annotation.surface: Hot oil spilling from a pool beside an island.
annotation.walkthrough: The H stays at the front and the I at the end; only OILPOOL moves.
annotation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi, Greek for 'the many', means the common people, the riff-raff.

entries.clue: Idiots notice person being evaluated (8)

annotation.surface: Fools pinning up a notice about someone under review.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a noun, a posted notice; it is the verb, to see.
annotation.definitionFit: The -ee suffix marks the one on the receiving end, as with employee, so this is whoever undergoes the evaluation.

entries.clue: Uniform patio rebuilt in ideal situation (6)

indicators.note: the letters of 'patio' are built again in a new order

blocks.note: U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A smoothly rebuilt patio makes the perfect setting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like an adjective describing the patio; it is the radio code word for U.
annotation.definitionFit: From Thomas More's imagined perfect island, the word now names any perfect state of affairs.

entries.clue: Draw a tense region (7)

blocks.note: a tract of land is a region

annotation.surface: Sketching a nervous-looking area.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous; it is the grammatical term, shortened to T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean pulling people or things towards you, as a show draws a crowd.

entries.clue: Caught turf accountants removing first of biscuits (7)

indicators.note: take away the first letter, B

blocks.note: a turf accountant is a bookmaker, a bookie
BOOKIES loses its first letter, the B that begins 'biscuits'

annotation.surface: Racetrack bookmakers caught pinching the first of the biscuits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Biscuits' does double work: its first letter, B, is the one removed from BOOKIES, and the whole word is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: what Americans call a cookie, the British call a biscuit.

entries.clue: Dances about on air? (6)

blocks.note: air is a gas, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: People dancing as if walking on air.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that air is only an example of a gas.
annotation.definitionFit: The conga is a dance done in a snaking line.

entries.clue: Starts to go loopy during month in rainforest (6)

indicators.note: take the first letters of 'go loopy'
the letters go inside the month

blocks.note: first letters of go and loopy

annotation.surface: Going crazy one month in the rainforest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starts to go loopy' reads as someone beginning to crack; 'starts' asks for the first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A jungle is dense tropical forest.

entries.clue: Get beneath part of stadium (10)

blocks.note: a stand is a section of seating in a stadium

annotation.surface: Getting in under the stands at a stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get' reads as move or reach; it means grasp, as in 'I get it'.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: to grasp, as in 'I don't get the joke'.

entries.clue: Steer right into seedy bar (5)

indicators.note: 'into' means going inside, so the right letter is put inside the bar word

blocks.note: a dive is a seedy bar

annotation.surface: Turning a car straight into a rough bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steer right' sounds like a driving instruction; right is just R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean guiding a vehicle's direction from behind the wheel.

entries.clue: Predict unpleasant aroma by outskirts of Dundee (4)

indicators.note: take the outer letters of 'Dundee'

annotation.surface: Forecasting a bad smell on the edge of Dundee.
annotation.walkthrough: Dundee is a city in eastern Scotland; its outskirts are just its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To bode is to foretell, as in 'bode ill'.

entries.clue: Cat couples audibly (4)

indicators.note: the answer sounds like the word for couples

annotation.surface: Cats pairing up noisily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Couples' reads as pairs of cats; it is the verb, links.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a wild cat with tufted ears and a stubby tail.

entries.clue: Leaving medal hanging around middle of stick (5)

indicators.note: to hang around something is to stay about it on all sides, so the medal word surrounds the letter
the central letter of 'stick'

blocks.note: gong is British slang for a medal

annotation.surface: A retirement medal hangs on a stick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaving medal' reads as a farewell award; 'leaving' is the definition and the medal is a gong, British slang for a decoration.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe departing, as in 'I'm going now'.

entries.clue: A foolish sheep rejected plant (9)

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the letters are sent back the way they came

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep

annotation.surface: A daft sheep turning its nose up at a plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' applies only to the foolish sheep; the opening A stays where it is.
annotation.definitionFit: The amaryllis is a bulb plant with large trumpet flowers.

entries.clue: Toothless attendee moving about (8)

indicators.note: the letters of 'attendee' move about

annotation.surface: A gummy guest wandering around a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Toothless' suggests weak or ineffective; here it is literal, the zoology word.
annotation.definitionFit: Edentate means lacking teeth, as sloths and anteaters are.

entries.clue: Arouse old jerk returning by Eurostar at first (6)

indicators.note: TIC comes back the other way
take the first letter of 'Eurostar'

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk

annotation.surface: An old fool coming home on the Eurostar stirs things up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' reads as an idiot; it is a twitch. Eurostar is the Channel Tunnel train between London and Paris.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to stir up feeling or interest.
